and the competitive landscape of the high-volume, low price (HVLP) fitness industry continues to weigh on the company’s share price.
The stock is down ~18% week-over-week and has already lost 60% of its value so far this year.
For the most recently reported quarter, Planet Fitness
beat EPS estimates and generated 7% more in sales during the quarter, but the growth came with higher operating costs and increased advertising expenses.
The company’s CEO also acknowledged that more effort needs for “sustainable member growth” a dynamic that reflects increased competition from new entrants in the fitness space.

“While PLNT has some important advantages given its large geographic footprint and generally stable base of franchisee operators, our view is that it may be incrementally difficult for the company to advance its growth strategy if consumers pivot toward a more experiential-oriented HVLP experience – one where price is not necessarily the most important factor when choosing a gym membership,” writes Deutsche Bank analyst Chris Woronka in his note to clients on Monday.

Woronka warns of the proliferation of HVLP gyms that are differentiating themselves through group classes, recovery spaces, social areas, and an ambiance that appeals to younger gym members, while at the same time, GLP-1 use by older cohorts keeps the growth trajectory of gyms like Planet Fitness stagnant.

“The challenge for PLNT, as we see it, is that it may be exceedingly difficult for the company to more closely match what key competitors are doing since 90% of its units are franchised,” Woronka adds.

Stagnant membership growth was also reflected in Q2 results and is behind the stock’s poor performance this year. Management acknowledged that higher same-club sales were largely a result of a price hike to its Classic Membership ($15 from $10) and not increased membership. Moreover, the price hike most turned potential members to competitively-priced rivals.
And its core customer seeking a “Judgement Free Zone” might have been turned off by a recent ad campaign.
“Planet Fitness noted that its recent marketing message which was geared towards more hard core fitness customers may have detracted from the company’s core customer base,”

With membership growth stalling, competitors raising the bar, and recent pricing and marketing moves failing to lure in new members, the company needs to find a way to make its value proposition resonate, or else its turnaround could be an uphill climb.

title: Running in place? Planet Fitness faces membership shrinkage as rivals gain ground
